newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia interior minister shakes off spy scandal.
newsitem.headline: Colombia interior minister shakes off spy scandal.

text.p: Interior Minister Horacio Serpa, President Ernesto Samper's right-hand man, shook off fallout from a growing spy scandal to win an overwhelming confidence vote in the Colombian Congress on Wednesday.

The opposition Conservative Party proposed the no-confidence motion after the local press reported that Serpa had taken part in secret talks to pave the way for German-brokered peace talks with leftist guerrillas and Colombian drug barons this year.

The meetings were set up by Werner Mauss, a shadowy German private eye with links to his country's secret services. He was charged with abduction after being arrested in northwest Colombia three weeks ago as he tried to smuggle a rebel kidnap victim out of the country.
Colombian authorities said Mauss is an international member of the National Liberation Army (ELN) guerrilla force. The German government said he was on a humanitarian mission.
Despite the Conservative effort to call Serpa to account for what they see as his murky dealings with foreign agents, the Liberal Party-controlled congress voted 169 to 41 in favour of Serpa.

Many political analysts saw the vote as strong backing for Serpa's likely bid for the presidency in 1998. He has not yet announced his candidacy but as Samper's closest ally in the government he has emerged as a natural heir to the president's brand of neoliberal and populist politics.
In recent congressional debates, Serpa has demonstrated flair in summoning up the loyalty of an otherwise divided Liberal Party.
